problem:
Consider the linear transformation
$T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}6x-4y \\ 2x-y \\ -5x+3y\end{aligned}]$ and the vectors 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Which of the given vectors belong to $\text{Ker}(T)?$
worked_solution:
A vector $u$ belongs to the kernel of a linear transformation $T$ if $T(u)=0.$ 

Therefore, we need to compute $T({v}_{i})$ for each ${v}_{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T({v}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ T({v}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 4 \\ -9\end{aligned}] \\ T({v}_{3}) & =T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\,T({v}_{i})\ne 0$ for any $i$'s, we conclude that none of them belongs to the kernel of $\,T.$

choices.value: None of the given vectors belong to the kernel of $T$
